abstract.para: For automated installations, &agama; relies on a profile, which is a configuration file that specifies how the system should be set up. This profile describes various aspects of the installation, including partitioning, networking, software selection, and other options. The concept of using a profile for automated installation is similar to &ay;. &agama; focuses specifically on the installation process itself and delegates further system configuration to other tools. &agama; aims for a high level of backward compatibility with &ay; profiles for automated installations.

note.title: Difference between &agama; and &ay; profiles
note.para: &agama; and &ay; profiles are largely compatible for all common use cases. However, &agama; profiles are not fully compatible with &ay; profiles, and cannot be used as a drop-in replacement without checking the compatibility. There are certain aspects of the &ay; profiles that are currently supported in &agama; profiles, or may be supported in the future. However, there are certain other aspects that are neither currently supported in &agama; profiles, nor will be supported in the future. For more information, refer to Using &ay; Profiles with &agama;.

section.title: Introduction to the &agama; profile structure
section.para: The &agama; profile configuration is defined using a JSON document. It contains several sections that are necessary for describing the installation parameters for a customized system. At a high level, the profile consists of the following sections:

callout.para: product: Identifies the OS/product to be installed.
root: Root credentials for administrative access.
l10n: Locale, keyboard, and time zone settings.
software: Packages and patterns to be installed.
bootloader: Boot loader config and kernel params.
security: SSL certs and other security settings.
legacyAutoyastStorage: Support for legacy &ay; JSON-style storage.
access: Remote access to the installed system over SSH and the &agama; web console.
questions: Predefined answers for questions the installer would otherwise ask interactively.

section.para: You can also describe profiles using Jsonnet, which is a superset of JSON. Jsonnet offers features like variables, functions and more convenient syntax, making profiles more readable, concise, and dynamic for injecting hardware information at runtime.
For more information on the JSON and Jsonnet profiles, refer to the resources mentioned in . The upstream resources usually contain the most up-to-date information and examples about the profiles.
